title: Why Gladiators Were Fat Vegetarians
hook: Gladiators weren't shredded bodybuilders—they were stuffed with barley and bean porridge.

scenes.text: Hollywood films always depict Roman gladiators with chiseled abs and low body fat. But forensic archaeology proves that's completely false.
scenes.imagePrompt: Dramatic sandy arena floor of the Colosseum with towering empty stone arches under a hot Mediterranean sky. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Hollywood films always depict Roman gladiators with chiseled abs and low body fat. But forensic archaeology proves that's completely false.

scenes.text: Chemical analysis of bones from a gladiator cemetery in Ephesus revealed they ate an almost entirely vegetarian diet based on barley and legumes.
scenes.imagePrompt: Terracotta bowls filled with hulled barley grain, dried fava beans, and coarse wheat flour on a rustic wooden table. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Chemical analysis of bones from a gladiator cemetery in Ephesus revealed they ate an almost entirely vegetarian diet based on barley and legumes.

scenes.text: Romans called them 'hordearii'—literally 'barley-men'. Their trainers deliberately fattened them up with thick carbohydrate porridge.

scenes.voicedText: Romans called them 'hordearii'—literally 'barley-men'. Their trainers deliberately fattened them up with thick carbohydrate porridge.

scenes.text: A thick layer of subcutaneous fat was vital armor: it absorbed flesh cuts without exposing nerves, major blood vessels, or vital organs.

scenes.text: Bloody surface cuts looked dramatic to cheering crowds while keeping the valuable trained fighters alive to compete another day.
